items.summary: ضربة منتظرة تهدد الهلال
items.body: ضربة منتظرة تهدد الهلال تسيطر حالة من القلق على الإيطالي سيموني إنزاجي، مدرب الهلال السعودي، بسبب الإصابة التي تعرض لها لاعبه البرتغالي روبن نيفيز خلال مواجهة الفتح التي انتهت بفوز الزعيم بهدفين دون رد، ضمن منافسات الجولة الثانية عشرة من دوري روشن السعودي. وتشير المعطيات الأولية أن نيفيز يعاني من إصابة في أسفل عضلات البطن، وسيغيب عن الملاعب لمدة تتراوح من 3 إلى 4 أسابيع. اقرأ أيضًا.. رونالدو يصفع جيسوس 3 مرات.. كواليس نارية وراء القرار التاريخي لكن يمكن أن تطول هذه الفترة، لأن بحسب برنامج " دورينا غير "، فإن نيفيز قد يخضع لعملية جراحية، لأن الإصابة التي يعاني منها في أسفل عضلات البطن، تعد من الإصابات الصعبة". وأوضح: "حال خضع نيفيز لعملية جراحية، فإن مدة غيابه عن الملاعب قد تمتد لفترة أطول، خاصة وأن الهلال لم يعلن حتى هذه اللحظة مدة غيابه". ناقش الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة ويعد نيفيز أحد أبرز وأهم نجوم دوري روشن والعالم في مركزه، بفضل المستويات المذهلة التي يقدمها منذ وصوله للهلال في صيف 2023. وشارك نيفيز (29 عامًا) في 14 مباراة خلال منافسات الموسم الحالي، سجل خلالها 9 أهداف وقدم 4 تمريرات حاسمة بمختلف المسابقات المحلية والقارية. تذاكر مباريات دوري روشن السعودي اشتر تذكرتك الآن!

items.summary: "Pre-EA, we never cancelled a project."
items.body: Ultima creator Richard Garriott was one of several developers on a recent panel hosted by the Georgia Game Developers Association, and Lord British was in fine form. Calling himself the "great-grandpa" of the group, he began by summarizing the current problems faced by the videogame industry. "It's not just one thing," Garriott began. "I think if it was one thing it would be a lot easier to diagnose and come back from, but it's a lot of folks who don't understand videogames trying to make money off of videogames, it's a political climate, it's a billion things. All the threads have woven together into this horrible knot that we're seeing now." He went on to describe a cycle he's seen play out multiple times over his years in the industry, where a technological advance comes along and everyone races to make a simple game that highlights that advance—whether it's the CD-ROM or a 3D-rendering pipeline or the internet—and only in the short gaps between these leaps forward is there much demand for something deeper. items.title: Sam Altman is annoyed his DRAM comment was 'taken out of context'
items.summary: Him being annoyed has not made DRAM cheaper, however.
items.body: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on a recent podcast that "from a global allocation perspective, actually it's quite terrible to have everyone have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and be used 5% of the time." Altman was talking about people running AI models locally rather than relying on data centers, which allow RAM usage to be maxed out in this "very supply-constrained environment." What many heard and responded to—PC gamers in particular—was resentment directed at those of us who don't run AI companies, but would still like to have and use our own personal computers, as a treat. (Image credit: Sam Altman) In an exchange on X this week, Altman said that his remark was "taken out of context" and that he actually wants "the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers." "I have been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time," Altman said. Altman's argument for increased memory production is no consolation to the tech enthusiasts and gamers who've been priced out of new hardware by his company and the rest of the AI industry. items.title: New Blood CEO would rather shut down the boomer shooter studio than sell out: 'In 20 years, we're done. I'm gonna say goodbye, shut it down'
items.summary: "I want us to have a happy ending. I want us to go out on our terms."
items.body: New Blood Interactive has been around for more than a decade—it's celebrating its 12 year anniversary, in fact—and is still going strong. Dusk, Gloomwood, Amid Evil, Fallen Aces, Ultrakill—it's got an enviable catalogue that continues to grow. But CEO Dave Oshry is still imagining how it might end. By keeping the studio relatively small, letting everyone work remotely, and not putting all its eggs in a franchise basket and spitting out endless sequels, it's been able to keep doing its thing. And that's the only way Oshry wants it to work. "If we couldn't be successful doing it this way, I wouldn't want to do it at all," he tells us. In short, it's taking a Steam-ish approach: no outright bans on AI content, but it's compulsory to disclose where it's been used in your mods, and to what extent. "An outright ban will not eliminate AI from the modding process but will prevent people from mentioning its use", wrote Nexus owner Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann in an update yesterday. "We'd prefer the opposite; it should be out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated according to the rules that we can implement on our platform". So, starting yesterday, modders uploading new projects to Nexus will have to tick a box declaring how much AI was used in their work, including promotional materials.
